zh: in a way that might cause somebody to roll their eyes, because they are annoyed or do not believe or approve of something
en: in a way that might cause somebody to roll their eyes, because they are annoyed or do not believe or approve of something
ex: The plot was eye-rollingly predictable.
该情节是可预测的。

zh: （高得）难以想象的；令人心痛的；催人落泪的
en: so high or extreme that it is difficult or painful to think about it
ex: eye-watering fare increases
超乎想象的交通票价飙升

zh: （高得）难以想象的；令人心痛的；催人落泪的
en: in a way that is so high or extreme that it is difficult or painful to think about it
ex: eye-wateringly high interest rates
难以承受的高利率

zh: used to refer to the number of people who visit a website, watch a television programme, read a magazine, etc., especially when considering how much money they may bring in
en: the whole of the eye, including the round part inside the head that cannot be seen
ex: It's a sad fact that bad news grabs more eyeballs than good news.
可悲的事实是，坏消息比好消息吸引了更多的眼球。

en: a small container that you put a liquid in to wash your eye with
the line of hair above the eye
ex: Ellen looked at me with a raised eyebrow.
埃伦扬起眉毛看着我。

en: a type of make-up in the form of a pencil, used for emphasizing or improving the shape of the eyebrows
a small container that you put a liquid in to wash your eye with

zh: 悦目的人（或物）；美人；好看的东西
en: an amount of something such as liquid or dust that has been thrown, or blown into your eye
ex: an eyeful of sand
一眼沙

en: a lens for one eye used to help you see more clearly with that eye
ex: a jeweller’s eyeglass
珠宝商的眼镜

en: one of the hairs growing on the edge of the eyelids
ex: false eyelashes
假睫毛

en: a hole with a metal ring around it in a piece of cloth or leather, normally used for passing a rope or string through
ex: Insert the tent poles through the eyelets on the groundsheet.
将帐篷杆穿过接地板上的孔眼。

en: either of the pieces of skin above and below the eye that cover it when you blink or close the eye
ex: She lifted one eyelid to see what he was doing.
她抬起一只眼皮看看他在做什么。

en: the direction that somebody is looking in
a type of make-up, usually black, that is put around the edge of the eyes to make them more attractive and likely to attract attention
ex: I had on heavy black eyeliner and black lipstick.
我涂了浓密的黑色眼线笔和黑色唇膏。
